tickerText: [TENNIS] Iva Jovic defends the Guadalajara Open with a 6-4, 6-2 win over Peyton Stearns on Sept. 21, going through the week without dropping a set for her second WTA 500 title • [SQUASH] Monday's PSA rankings make 19-year-old Amina Orfi the youngest women's world No. 1 after her Qatar Classic five-set final over Hania El Hammamy, while Mostafa Asal swept Victor Crouin for his 30th tour title • [BADMINTON] Asian Games Day 4 in Aichi-Nagoya pits India's women's and men's teams against Japan in team quarterfinals on Sept. 22, with PV Sindhu opening against Akane Yamaguchi and a medal guaranteed for the winner • [PICKLEBALL] Championship Sunday at the Veolia Arizona Open leaves Christopher Haworth and Anna Leigh Waters with singles gold while Alshon/Daescu and Rohrabacher/Todd take doubles; the PPA Tour heads to Las Vegas Sept. 28 • [TABLE TENNIS] Asian Games team play continues Sept. 22 with India's women facing Thailand in the round of 16 and the men in knockout action after sweeping Pakistan, plus mixed doubles and evening quarterfinals in Nagoya

newsItems.title: Jovic Defends Guadalajara
newsItems.excerpt: Iva Jovic beat Peyton Stearns 6-4, 6-2 on Sept. 21 to successfully defend her Guadalajara Open title without dropping a set, becoming the first back-to-back singles champion at the WTA 500 event.

newsItems.title: Orfi Hits World No. 1
newsItems.excerpt: Amina Orfi becomes the youngest women's world No. 1 in Monday's PSA rankings after winning the Qatar Classic, while Mostafa Asal's straight-games final over Victor Crouin completes his sweep of every current major title.

newsItems.title: India Faces Japan in QFs
newsItems.excerpt: Both Indian badminton teams meet hosts Japan in Asian Games quarterfinals on Sept. 22 in Aichi-Nagoya, with Sindhu versus Yamaguchi headlining the women's tie and Lakshya Sen's squad following in the afternoon.

newsItems.title: Arizona Open Crowns Set
newsItems.excerpt: Christopher Haworth and Anna Leigh Waters won singles at the Veolia Arizona Open on Sept. 20 in Mesa, with Alshon/Daescu and Rohrabacher/Todd taking doubles gold on a $1.06M PPA Championship Sunday.
